package.title: 100 NAT-IE-Style Waves and Optics MCQs with Explanations

questions.question: A wave travels at 24 m/s and has a frequency of 6 Hz. What is its wavelength?
A wave completes 5 oscillations in 2 seconds. What is its frequency?
What is the period of a wave with frequency 8 Hz?
A wave has a wavelength of 0.5 m and a frequency of 12 Hz. What is its speed?
Two points on a travelling wave are one complete wavelength apart. What is their phase difference?
Which type of wave has oscillations perpendicular to its direction of travel?
In a longitudinal wave, what are compressions?
choices: Regions where particles are closer together

questions.question: A wave's frequency doubles while its speed in the same medium remains constant. What happens to its wavelength?
Which quantity describes the maximum displacement of an oscillating particle from its equilibrium position?
A wave has a period of 0.04 s. What is its frequency?
A wave travels 15 m in 3 s. What is its speed?
A ripple has a wavelength of 0.8 m and a speed of 4 m/s. What is its frequency?
A source produces 60 waves in 12 seconds. What is the period?
A wave has frequency 10 Hz and wavelength 3 m. How far does it travel in 2 seconds?
When a wave passes from one medium into another, which property stays the same if the source frequency is unchanged?
A wave's frequency is 50 Hz. How many complete cycles occur in 4 seconds?
If the period of an oscillation increases, what happens to its frequency?
choices: It increases in the same proportion

questions.question: A transverse wave has a wavelength of 2 m and frequency 3 Hz. What distance does it travel in 5 seconds?
Which statement about energy carried by a travelling wave is generally correct?
choices: The wave transfers energy without requiring a net transfer of the medium
The wave permanently carries every particle forward
Energy can travel only in a vacuum

questions.question: Two waves in the same medium have the same frequency but different amplitudes. Which quantity must be the same?
Sound in ordinary air is primarily which type of wave?
A sound wave travels at 340 m/s and has a frequency of 170 Hz. What is its wavelength?
A sound wave has a frequency of 250 Hz. What is its period?
Which property of a sound wave is most directly associated with how high or low a note sounds?
Which change most directly makes a sound louder, with frequency unchanged?
choices: Decreasing its wavelength in a different medium

questions.question: A person hears an echo 2 seconds after making a sound. If sound travels at 340 m/s, how far away is the reflecting surface?
Why can sound not travel through a perfect vacuum?
choices: It requires a material medium to transmit mechanical vibrations
Vacuum absorbs all sound energy by reflection

questions.question: A sound source moves toward a stationary listener. What is the usual Doppler-effect change heard by the listener?
What happens to the speed of sound in a uniform medium when the sound's frequency changes?
choices: It changes in direct proportion to frequency

questions.question: An echo returns after 0.6 s. If the sound speed is 330 m/s, what is the distance to the reflecting wall?
A sound wave travels at 300 m/s and has a wavelength of 1.5 m. What is its frequency?
Which statement correctly compares infrasonic and ultrasonic sound?
choices: Infrasound is below 20 Hz; ultrasound is above 20,000 Hz
Infrasound is above 20,000 Hz; ultrasound is below 20 Hz
Both are audible to every human
Both describe sound travelling in a vacuum

questions.question: A string vibrates at 120 Hz. What is the frequency of the sound it produces in air, assuming steady vibration?
choices: The speed of sound in air

questions.question: In the same medium, what happens to sound wavelength if its frequency decreases while speed remains constant?
A sound wave has a frequency of 680 Hz and travels at 340 m/s. How many wavelengths fit into a 10 m distance?
Which electromagnetic wave has the longest wavelength among these options?
Which electromagnetic wave has the highest frequency among these options?
What is the approximate speed of electromagnetic waves in a vacuum?
Which statement about electromagnetic waves in a vacuum is correct?
choices: They are transverse and can travel without a material medium
They are longitudinal and require air
Their speed depends on their amplitude

questions.question: Which radiation is commonly used in remote controls?
Which electromagnetic radiation is commonly used to image bones in a medical radiograph?
Which electromagnetic radiation is commonly used in microwave ovens to heat food?
Which visible-light colour has the longest wavelength in the usual spectrum?
Which visible-light colour has the highest frequency among these options?
If electromagnetic radiation has frequency 6 × 10¹⁴ Hz in vacuum, what is its approximate wavelength?
Which statement about all electromagnetic waves in a vacuum is correct?
choices: They travel at the same speed
They all have the same frequency
They all have the same wavelength

questions.question: Which part of the electromagnetic spectrum is commonly associated with sterilising some surfaces and causing sunburn?
A beam of light strikes a plane mirror at 35° to the normal. What is the angle of reflection?
A light ray makes an angle of 20° with a plane mirror's surface. What is its angle of incidence?
An object is 3 m in front of a plane mirror. How far behind the mirror is its image?
Which image property is characteristic of a plane mirror?
choices: Virtual, upright, and the same size as the object
Real, upright, and the same size

questions.question: A person stands 2 m from a plane mirror. What is the distance between the person and their image?
A ray strikes a plane mirror at an incidence angle of 50°. What angle does the reflected ray make with the mirror surface?
For regular reflection from a smooth plane surface, the incident ray, reflected ray, and normal lie in:
A plane mirror is rotated by 10° while the incident ray stays fixed. By how much does the reflected ray rotate?
Which mirror is commonly used to provide a wider field of view in a vehicle's side mirror?
An object is placed beyond the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. Where does its real image form?
choices: Between the focus and centre of curvature

questions.question: An object is at the centre of curvature of a concave mirror. What is the image?
choices: Real, inverted, and the same size at C
Virtual, upright, and larger behind the mirror
Real, upright, and smaller at F

questions.question: An object is placed between the focus and pole of a concave mirror. What image is formed?
A spherical mirror has a radius of curvature of 40 cm. What is the magnitude of its focal length?
A ray parallel to the principal axis strikes a concave mirror. After reflection, it passes through:
choices: The pole at every incidence point

questions.question: A ray directed through the centre of curvature of a spherical mirror strikes the mirror. What is its direction after reflection?
choices: It travels parallel to the principal axis

questions.question: The refractive index of a transparent material is defined as:
choices: Speed of light in vacuum divided by speed in the material
Speed in the material divided by speed in vacuum
Wavelength in the material divided by wavelength in vacuum

questions.question: Light travels through a material at 2 × 10⁸ m/s. What is the material's refractive index?
A ray enters glass from air at an angle of incidence of 30°. The glass has refractive index 1.5 and air is taken as 1. What is sin of the refraction angle?
Light travels from air into a medium with a higher refractive index at a nonzero incidence angle. In which direction does it bend?
choices: Along the surface in every case

questions.question: Light enters a lower-index medium from a higher-index medium at a nonzero incidence angle, without total internal reflection. Which way does it bend?
choices: It always travels along the normal

questions.question: At normal incidence, a light ray passes from air into glass. What happens to its direction?
choices: It continues along the same line, though its speed changes
It reflects completely in every case

questions.question: Which condition is required for total internal reflection?
choices: Light travels from higher to lower refractive index and incidence exceeds the critical angle
Light travels from lower to higher refractive index at any angle
Incidence is zero in any medium
The two media have identical refractive indices

questions.question: A glass has refractive index 1.5 and is surrounded by air of index 1. What is the sine of its critical angle?
Why can a ray of light be guided along an optical fibre?
choices: Repeated total internal reflection at the core boundary
Repeated refraction into the surrounding air
Absorption and re-emission at each point
Diffraction by the fibre's outer surface

questions.question: When light enters glass from air, which property remains unchanged at the boundary?
Light has wavelength 600 nm in air and enters a material of refractive index 1.5. Approximately what is its wavelength in the material?
A rectangular glass slab has parallel opposite faces. For a ray entering and leaving into the same surrounding medium, how is the emergent ray oriented relative to the incident ray?
An object is 30 cm from a converging lens with focal length 10 cm. Using 1/f = 1/do + 1/di, what is the image distance?
An object is placed at twice the focal length from a converging lens. Where does its image form?
choices: At twice the focal length on the other side
At the focal point on the same side

questions.question: An object is placed inside the focal length of a converging lens. What kind of image is formed?
choices: Real, upright, and the same size

questions.question: Which lens is thinner at its centre than at its edges and generally diverges parallel incident rays?
A converging lens has focal length 25 cm. What is its optical power in dioptres?
A lens has optical power −2 D. What is its focal length?
A converging lens forms a real image 40 cm from the lens when an object is 20 cm away. What is the focal length?
A 2 cm tall object forms a 6 cm tall image. What is the magnitude of the magnification?
A lens forms a real image of an object. With the usual real-is-positive image-distance convention, what is the sign of the image distance?
choices: It must equal the focal length

questions.question: An object is 12 cm from a converging lens of focal length 18 cm. What is the image distance using 1/f = 1/do + 1/di?
A concave mirror has focal length 15 cm. What is its radius of curvature magnitude?
A concave mirror has focal length 12 cm and an object is 36 cm in front. Using 1/f = 1/do + 1/di, how far from the mirror is the image?
A convex mirror is used to view a larger area behind a vehicle. What kind of image does it form for a real object?
choices: Virtual, inverted, and the same size

questions.question: A ray parallel to the principal axis passes through a thin converging lens. After refraction, it travels through:
choices: The principal focus on the far side
The optical centre without deviation in every case
The focus on the incident side
The centre of curvature of a mirror

questions.question: A ray passes through the optical centre of an ideal thin lens. What is its approximate direction after passing through?
choices: It always passes through the focus

questions.question: Which defect of vision is commonly corrected using a diverging lens?
Which type of lens is commonly used to correct hypermetropia?
A simple magnifying glass is normally used with the object placed:
choices: Within the focal length of a converging lens
At the centre of curvature of a mirror
Beyond the focal length of a diverging lens

questions.question: A camera uses a converging lens to form an image of a distant object on its sensor. The image is generally:
choices: Always the same size as the object

questions.question: An object is placed at the focal point of an ideal converging lens. Where do the emerging rays meet?
A converging lens has power +5 D. What is its focal length?
Two thin converging lenses of powers +2 D and +3 D are in contact. What is their combined power?
Which statement about a real image formed by a converging lens is correct?
choices: It can be projected onto a screen
It must be on the same side as the object

questions.question: A 3 cm object is 15 cm from a converging lens; its real image forms 30 cm away. What is the image height magnitude?
A thin lens has focal length 0.5 m. What is its power?
A ray of light enters a glass prism and white light spreads into a spectrum. What is the main cause of this dispersion?
choices: Different wavelengths refract by different amounts
All wavelengths have identical refractive indices
The prism changes light into sound
The glass reflects every colour equally
